Referred to Committee on Finance (Budget Allocation).

REPORT OF COMMITTEE ON FINANCE
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:
Your Committee on Finance, as required by our Code, has reviewed the audited
financial statements presented by the Grand Treasurer for the fiscal year ended
June 30, 1985.
Approval by the Grand Master for supplementary appropriations in the
amount of $101,777 has been given to cover those items where budgets were
exceeded; of that figure $8,000 was to cover increased costs for the California Freemason Magazine.
Costs for the publication and distribution of our California Freemason
Magazine for the 1985-1986 year are estimated at $182,700. To cover these
costs an increase of$ .IO in the per capita will be required. We believe this
Magazine is of great benefit to the Craft and do not hesitate to recommend
this increase.
The rate of reimbursement for the use of personal vehicles on Grand Lodge
business shall remain at $ .18 per mile until this time again in 1986.
New capital additions have been budgeted in the amount of $34,500 as
shown below:
Computer Terminal and Typewriters .................. $ 6,500
Computer System Upgrade .......................... $28,000
Total ............................................. $34,500
The capital addition to upgrade our computer system is necessary because
of the obsolescense of our present system and more requests within Grand
Lodge and constituent Lodges for additional information. Proper implementation of the system will take several years, using a phased approach. Phase
one is budgeted for $28,000.

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

The total budgeted expenses for the 1985-1986 fiscal year have increased
less than one percent over the 1984-1985 fiscal year. However, the per capita
tax has increased from $5.84 to $6.30. This increase in per capia results primarily from our continuing loss of membership. For fiscal year 1984-1985 the per
capita tax was based on a membership of 173,500. For the current fiscal year
per capita is based on a projected membership of 166,500. This represents
a decline of 4 percent or 7,000 members. Unless we are able to reverse the
decline in membership the per capita tax will continue to increase even if expenses are held constant.
Your Finance Committee foresees that in the near future the decline in
membership will continue to significantly impact your per capita tax.
Although your Committee on Finance is principally interested in, and
charged with the responsibility of establishing a budget for the operational
expenses of the Grand Lodge, we are also very concerned with the control
of those expenses. We note that the expenditures necessary to hold our Annual Communicatio n is a major budget item. A substantial portion of that
expenditure is for lodging and other expenses of Grand Lodge officers, Inspectors and Committeemen . We believe that all avenues of potential cost
reduction should be pursued.
In the past we have provided all Lodge Secretaries with advance notice of
the proposed per capita asessment following our August budget meeting with
the Grand Lodge Elective Line. This year we also provided copies for the
Master and Wardens and requested that it be read in Lodge.
Our sincere thanks to the Very Worshipful John A. Sickenberger, Grand
Treasurer, for his expert counseling in the area of Grand Lodge fiscal affairs
and to Brother Hugo Delfin, our Accounting Manager and his staff for their
fine assistance.
Our thanks also to the Very Worshipful Robert A. Klinger, Grand Secretary,
and his staff for their support.
The proposed 1985-1986 budget is presented here in summary form. Details
are also published in the Proceedings as part of the report.

AFTERNOON SESSION - WEDNESDAY, OCTOBER 16, 1985
Members and guests assembled at 3:00 P.M. for the open installation of
the Officers elected and appointed to serve for the ensuing Grand Lodge year,
Grand Master Roy J. Henville presiding.

278

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

INSTALLATION OF OFFICERS

Following the Benediction the assembled guests retired for a reception to
greet the newly installed Grand Lodge Officers.

The Installation Ceremony commenced at 3:00 P.M., with the retiring Grand
Master, Roy J. Henville, acting as Installing Officer, and Past Grand Master
Raymond A. Ebbage acting as Master of Ceremonies. The Appointive Officers were introduced and duly installed after which the Grand Lecturer,
Grand Secretary and Grand Treasurer were also introduced and installed. The
Junior Grand Warden and Senior Grand Warden were then introduced and
installed in their respective stations. The Deputy Grand Master was then installed after which the Grand Master was duly installed.
The newly installed Grand Master was saluted with Public Grand Honors
and he was then presented with his first gavel by Brother Nick Kerhoulis P.M.
of Tehama Lodge No. 3. The newly installed Grand Master explained the
history of the Bible upon which he had been installed; he then requested the
Grand Marshal to escort Elinor Henville to the East where she was presented
with a beautiful bouquet of red roses by the newly installed Grand Master.
Past Grand Master Edward H. Siems then presented her with a gift on behalf
of the entire membership of the Fraternity. This gracious lady responded with
an expression of love and appreciation for the remembrances.
Past Grand Master Kermit A. Jacobson presented the Grand Master's Lapel
Pin to the retiring Grand Master. Past Grand Master E. Arthur Haglund
presented to the Junior Past Grand Master the Past Grand Master's Apron
following which Past Grand Master Harry L. Maynard presented the Past
Grand Master's Certificate. Appropriate words with expressions of gratitude
accompanied each of the above presentations.
The retiring Grand Master met with the newly installed Grand Master,
Deputy Grand Master and Senior and Junior Grand Wardens at the altar
where the Arthur S. Crites Lapel Pins designating their respective stations
were exchanged.
The Grand Master's daughters, Janet and Pamela, presented their father
with a beautiful "Lone Star Belt Buckle." The newly installed Grand Master
requested all of the wives of the newly installed Grand Lodge officers to stand
for recognition, after which members of Capital City Lodge No. 499 were
recognized. Grand Master John W. Driskell then addressed the assembled
guests. He elaborated on some of the programs which he will pursue during
the forthcoming year. He expressed his appreciation to all in attendance for
being with him on this occasion.
At the conclusion of the Grand Masters installation message he was accorded a standing ovation.
Special thanks were extended to Organist Harold M. Hand and Soloist
Donald A. Nielsen for their beautiful musical selections, "Let There Be Peace
on Earth" and "You Will Never Walk Alone." A thank you was also extended
to the Potentate of Ben Ali Shrine Temple in Sacramento for hosting the
refreshments for the reception which was to follow.
All business of the 136th Annual Communication was completed at 4:05
P.M. after which the newly installed Grand Master announced that Grand
Lodge would be called on at 9:00 A.M. on Thursday, October 17, 1985 for
the purpose of Closing.

279

THURSDAY MORNING, October 17, 1985
At 9:00 A.M. Grand Lodge was called on for the purpose of closing, with
Grand Master John W. Driskell presiding. The Benediction was given by the
newly installed Grand Chaplain. All business being completed, Grand Lodge
was closed in due form at 9:10 A.M.

California, a nonprofit, public benefit corporation, as of June 30, 1985
and 1984, and the related statements of support, revenue and expenses
and changes in fund balances for the years then ended. Our examinations
were made in accordance with generally accepted au di ting standards and
accordingly included such tests of the accounting records and such other

In our opinion, the aforementioned financial statements present
fairly the financial position of The Masonic Homes of California at June
30, 1985 and 1984 and the results of its operations and changes in fund
balances for the years then ended, in conformity with generally accepted
accounting principles applied on a consistent basis.

NOTE 1 - SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES:
NOTE 1 - SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES:
The financial statements of Masonic Homes of California have been
Significant accounting
prepared on the accrual basis of accounting.
policies follow:
Fund Accounting:
To insure observance of limitations and restrictions placed on the
use of resources available to the Homes, the accounts of the Homes are
maintained in accordance with the principles of fund accounting.
The assets, liabilities and fund balances of the Homes are reported
in four self-balancing funds, as follow:
General Fund - Resources are available to support the operations of
the Homes at Union City and Covina, California.

Maintenance and repairs are charged to expense when incurred.

and equipment are capitalized.
On sale or retirement, the cost and
accumulated depreciation applicable thereto are eliminated from the
accounts and the differences between net book value and the proceeds from
sale or retirment are included in income.
Other Assets:
Other assets consist of life insurance policies, real estate and
mineral rights assigned or bequeathed to the Masonic Homes.

Permanent Endowment Fund - Ordinances of the Grand Lodge provide that
no portion of the principal of the Permanent Endowment Fund shall be
expended for any purpose and income from the principal shall be used
only for the maintenance and general operation of Masonic Homes.

Real estate and mineral rights are recorded at the nominal value of
$1 each for accountability. Payments by the Masonic Homes of obligations
of the assig~ors secured by these assets are added to the nominal value.

Hugo M. Lorber Masonic Home, Union City Fund - This fund provides for
the operation, preservation and betterment of the Home at Union City,
California.

Life insurance policies are recorded at their actuarily determined
present values.

Restricted Trust Funds - Details to these Trust Funds are contained
in Note 7 to the financial statements.
Investments in Securities:
Investments, consisting of marketable securities, are stated at fair
market values.
Changes in market values between reporting dates are
recognized for financial reporting.

NOTE 3 - NOTES RECEIVABLE:
Notes receivable represent notes from sales of real estate assigned
to the Masonic Homes by residents of Union City Home and sales of real
estate received as gifts or bequests. These notes are secured by deeds
of trust.
NOTE 4 - PENSION PLAN:
Masonic Homes of California, the Grand Lodge and component
organizations and California Masonic Memorial Temple contribute to the
California Masonic Retirement Plan, a defined benefit plan, for the
benefit of all eligible employees. The total pension expense of Masonic
Homes for the years ended June 30, 1965 and 1964 was $120, 102 and
$236,546, respectively.
The actuarial present value of accumulated Plan benefits at January
1, 1985 (the most recent determination date) was $2,988,569. The market
value of net Plan assets on the same date was $3,585,103.
Accumulated Plan benefits are those future periodic payments,
including lump-sl.111 distributions, that are expected to be provided, under
the Plan's provisions, to employees for services rendered.
Effective January 1, 1964, the actuarial cost method was changed to
the Entry Age cost method from the Aggregate Actuarial cost method and
the rate of return assumption was increased to 7% from 5%.

On November 27, 1974, Masonic Homes of California, in exchange for
conveyance of real property, entered into an agreement to pay the
conveyors during their lifetime $1 ,250 per month. The receipients are
presently 85 and 89 years old and the liability at June 30 equals the
present value of future estimated payments, based upon life
expectancies.
NOTE 6 - HUGO M. LORBER MASONIC HOME, UNION CITY FUND:
During 1962 and 1983, the Masonic Homes of California received
bequests from the Estate of Hugo M. Lorber in the amount of $11,680,365.
Mr. Lorber's Last Will and Testament provided that the bequest be used at
the Home for the elderly at Union City, California.
The Board of Trustees established the Hugo M. Lorber Masonic Home,
Union City Fund to account for the bequest and resolved that all income
from the Fund should be used for operating, rehab ill tating, preserving
and enhancing the Home for Adults at Union City, as deemed necessary.
The Board of Trustees also resolved that the Fund represented a
source for a!Wi tions and replacements of property at Union City, as
represented by the accumulation of depreciation.
NOTE 7 - RESTRICTED TRUST FUNDS:
Details to each trust fund, follow:
George F. and Laura E. Brigham Scholarship Fund:
The principal of this fund is held as a scholarship fund for the
benefit of the Covina Home residents, of which $25,000 may be loaned
for this purpose. Income of this fund is restricted and may be used
only for providing scholarships.
Mildred R. Brown and Leroy G. Brown Memorial Fund:
Principal and income from this fund are to be used for 'llaking
loans for educational purposes to children that the Board of Trustees
deems worthy.
